long_biography.plain_text:
At sixteen, Iwan Wirth staged an exhibition of paintings by the Swiss artist Bruno Gasser in a rented basement near St Gallen. He later worked as a private dealer in Zurich, learning the art trade through exhibitions and direct relationships with artists and collectors.

When the Zurich venture opened, Wirth built it with Manuela Wirth and Ursula Hauser. Rather than a solo project, its early development involved the three partners travelling to exhibitions, museums and studios and discussing art together. Ursula Hauser's private collection sometimes influenced their commercial interests, but it remained distinct from the gallery and included artists the business did not represent. Wirth subsequently combined art dealing with operational expansion as the enterprise established venues beyond Switzerland. That record supports both a founder and operator role without implying sole ownership of every gallery holding.
